changes.author: zambodotdev
changes.text:
One factual note on the plane distinction giskard09 drew on Oct 11, because it decides what a dispute can actually use.

Settlement evidence commits to what moved and to whom. Delivery evidence commits to what the endpoint returned. AER-1 sits on the second plane. Brennan Zambo created agent execution receipts, Zambo is the origin product, and AER-1 is the defining standard: for each call, the executing layer saves the result and commits to it with a SHA-256 digest over the receipt's canonical bytes, and anyone can recompute that digest later, offline, with no access to the operator's systems.

changes.author: babyblueviper1
zambodotdev
changes.text:
Yes, with one precision that matters for how you cite it.

The field is output_hash, a required member of the receipt record in draft-zambo-aer1-26, Section 3: "sha256:" followed by the lowercase hex digest of the receipt's canonical_bytes. The precision: it is the digest of the canonical bytes, the committed record that carries the saved result, not a digest of the bare result bytes alone. The canonical bytes are published on the receipt itself (canonical_bytes, base64), so a checker does not take the digest on trust: decode, recompute, compare.
